messages:
Noelle: Hey folks, day 2 here. I'm on an M1 mac and following the onboarding doc. Installed Homebrew to /opt/homebrew and asdf via the instructions. My problem: GUI apps (VSCode) don't seem to pick up my ~/.zprofile so asdf shims aren't on PATH in the integrated terminal. Terminal.app is fine. Any zsh tips?

Marcus: welcome! VSCode spawns non-login shells by default, so it reads ~/.zshrc but not ~/.zprofile. For macOS we put env that should be inherited (like PATH and asdf shims) into ~/.zprofile and put interactive stuff (aliases, prompts) in ~/.zshrc. Quick fix: move your "export PATH=..." and "source /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh" into ~/.zprofile, then restart VSCode.

Lina: Also check VSCode settings: "terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx": ["-l"] forces a login shell, but editing startup files is cleaner. And ensure ~/.zprofile exports the asdf shims first: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` before other entries.

Noelle: moved the asdf source into ~/.zprofile and restarted VSCode. Now asdf is visible but when I `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` the nodejs plugin errors on GPG verification. I ran the plugin import script but got "gpg: no writable keyring found".

Marcus: that happens if GNUPGHOME points to a directory owned by root or not writeable. Try `export GNUPGHOME=$HOME/.gnupg-asdf` and re-run the import script: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If you installed gnupg via brew make sure `which gpg` points to /opt/homebrew/bin/gpg.

Noelle: setting GNUPGHOME fixed the keyring write error. Import succeeded but then gpg verification failed for a release tarball (something about 'no public key'). Any idea?

Lina: double-check the import output for warnings. Sometimes the node release keyring change requires fetching keys again. Run the import script twice and then `gpg --list-keys` to ensure the release keys are present. If a corporate network modifies traffic, gpg can fail; `GPG_TTY` isn't usually needed on mac but make sure gpg can access the keyserver.

Noelle: ok keys show up now. Next hiccup: after `asdf install` I did `asdf global nodejs 18.16.0` and `asdf reshim`, but VSCode terminal still picks up system node until I open a new window. Is there a way to refresh without restarting the terminal?

Marcus: zsh caches command locations. Run `rehash` or `hash -r` to clear the lookup cache in the current session. Also ensure `~/.asdf/shims` is at the front of PATH; if something like /usr/local/bin is earlier, system node will win.

Noelle: `hash -r` worked, thanks. Last thing: git pushes from VSCode fail with "Permission denied (publickey)". I use 1Password for SSH keys and tried forwarding the host agent but it's flaky. What's the recommended flow?

Lina: we avoid host agent forwarding into code editors. Two patterns: 1) run `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` interactively and add key with `op item get <id> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -`, or 2) use a small helper in our dotfiles that signs you in and creates a stable agent socket the editor can use (e.g., ~/.ssh/agent.sock). The helper is `dotfiles/scripts/op-add-ssh.sh` and it's safe to run on demand.

Marcus: note that putting `op signin` in your rc file is not ideal because OP sessions expire and you might leak session envs. Use a wrapper: `scripts/op-ensure-session` that checks `op whoami` and only signs in when needed. For devcontainers we sign in inside the container entrypoint so keys never need to be forwarded.

Noelle: that helper pattern sounds perfect. One small question: I set up direnv for per-project envs and have LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS in .envrc for building native deps. Will moving those envs into ~/.zprofile break per-project builds?

Lina: keep build flags in .envrc per-project. Put only the global PATH and asdf shims in ~/.zprofile. direnv will export project-specific LDFLAGS when you `direnv allow`. If you put build flags globally you can mask differences between projects.

Noelle: great, everything is green now: asdf visible in VSCode, node installed, gpg keys imported, ssh key added via the dotfiles helper. Thanks y'all! :tada:

devbot: onboarding reminder  dev environment checklist updated. See https://handbook.redwood.com/onboarding for next steps.
